chapter: Fred Astaire and the high points
title: Playing Lyndon Johnson's inauguration; Hubert Humphrey
summary: He alternated with Vincent Lopez at the Statler; Humphrey danced with the wife of lawyer Hobart Taylor, later asked him for autographs for his daughters and invited him to a White House luncheon.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: Oh, that's very nice. Well, listen, about the inauguration, how did Sam lay that on?
You know, I don't know how that come through.
Or maybe they came to him.

That come through that guy Symington, Stuart or something like that, see. He was a Senator. Anyhow, it come through and they wanted me to play this thing, and I'm trying to think how it come through, but anyhow we wound up playing at the Statler with a fellow who had a band at the Taft Hotel for so many years. What is his name?
Vincent Lopez?
Vincent Lopez. Yeah, we were alternating, you know.
Yeah.
And then this was a fantastic thing, you know, you'd go to the boxes where the Senators sat, you know, and all that stuff.
Yeah, sure.
And here he comes in, him and Ladybird and -- or Humphrey, and his wife, you know, Mrs. Humphrey.
Yeah.
And right away he goes over and he gets

the black cat, Hobart Taylor, he was a lawyer, and grabs his wife. He don't dance with Ladybird. He grabs his wife, a pretty brown skinned woman, and he dances like an old hustler, you know, with them big feet. And he danced there by himself for awhile, you know. Then all the others joined in.
That's nice.

Then later on I met Humphrey at the London House, and he come by. He said, "I just had to come by and see you." He said, "I never asked nobody for an autograph in my life, but I want an autograph from you. I want two, for my daughters."
Well, I never. Isn't that nice.

So, you know, things like that. And then later I had a telegram. I have it there, and an invitation for luncheon. He was entertaining the King of Cameroon, or the President of Cameroon. And you go in by the east gate and all that kind of stuff. So I thought that was --
Did you play?
No, no playing, just to go there for lunch.
Very nice. Very nice.
It's an honor. It's different from when you're hired to play.
